geneal — default ablation (safety + diversity)

A: 5116 genes · B: 5116 genes · 1 cell lines · 1 seeds · K=10 · AL 2×5 · τ=0.5 (absolute) · contrast ACH-001360 · acq=ucb

How to read this

Two analyses, two questions, two toxicity definitions.

Reading method labels (compact [acq]·[filtering]·[tox]): G=greedy acquisition (UCB on efficacy), E=EHVI (dual-objective); nom=filter the final shortlist only, RT=per-round filtering (filter the candidate pool every round); K=known toxicity (oracle), P=predicted toxicity (learned GP). So G·nom·K = greedy acquisition + end-stage filter on known toxicity (= oracle ceiling); E·RT·P = EHVI + per-round filter on predicted toxicity. random/farthest/cluster/info-div are the no-safety baselines.

Safety rules (Analysis A). • greedy: top-K predicted efficacy, no safety. • filter · known: keep genes below the τ toxicity ceiling using the known toxicity (oracle limit). • filter · predicted: same ceiling, but toxicity is learned by a GP. • EHVI: learned toxicity with a dual-objective EHVI acquisition. • random / farthest / cluster / info_div: prior-work / naive baselines (info_div = informativeness+diversity, IterPert-like; greedy = quality-only, NAIAD-like). The known-toxicity filter is the limit the learned rules chase.

Filter timing (end-stage vs per-round). The filter can be applied only to the final shortlist (end-stage, nom) or at every acquisition round (RT), restricting each round to genes believed safe — so the assay budget isn't spent on genes we think are toxic. Acquisition and nomination remain distinct stages; per-round filtering constrains both.

Diversity operators (Analysis B). • none: top-K by quality. • k-DPP · embedding: quality-weighted k-DPP with the learned embedding-cosine similarity. • k-DPP · STRING: external STRING combined-score network similarity. • k-DPP · CORUM: external CORUM protein-complex (Jaccard co-membership) similarity. None is outcome similarity — the embedding-vs-STRING-vs-CORUM comparison is the similarity-source ablation (learned vs two external knowledge graphs, dense → sparse). Layered on the four safety-aware bases (G·nom·P / G·RT·P / E·nom·P / E·RT·P). A pathway-failure simulation quantifies the value of the resulting diversity.

Toxicity & τ. • contrast (primary): lethality in one fixed contrast line (normal-tissue stand-in). • aggregate: common-essential fraction, excluding the target line. τ is a quantile: the dashed line on each plot is the τ-quantile of the candidate toxicity (τ=0.5 = the safest half) — for the contrast definition, quantile(−effect in the contrast line, τ).
Naive greedy carries toxicity 1.00 at efficacy 1.40. The known-toxicity ceiling (trunc_known) reaches toxicity 0.14 / efficacy 0.82; the learned ceilings (trunc_pred 0.64, EHVI+trunc 0.32) sit between — the gap to trunc_known is the price of learning safety from the embedding. (Untruncated EHVI baseline: tox 0.91.)

Toxicity definition: contrast (primary)

Each point a method (mean over lines × seeds, 95% CI bars). Up = more lethal, left = safer. Dashed line = the τ toxicity ceiling (quantile 0.5 of candidate toxicity).

For each method, how many of the K nominees have TRUE toxicity below (permissible) vs above the τ ceiling. The naive/diversity baselines nominate many over-threshold (toxic) targets; the safety rules keep them permissible.

For the methods with no safety filter: the fraction of their K nominees that would pass at each hypothetical threshold τ (empirical CDF of nominee toxicity, pooled over lines). Curves that stay low until high τ are nominating toxic targets. Dashed line = the τ used in the main results.

A · Per-cell-line tradeoff

One panel per cell line; the same methods; each with its own τ ceiling. The safety ordering holds across lines.

A · Gene landscape — nominated targets per method (all lines pooled)

Each panel a method. Grey = all candidate genes (pooled over 1 lines); open circles = that method's 10 targets; dashed line = τ ceiling. Safety rules pull picks left of the ceiling.

B · Value of diversity — pathway-failure simulation

(Untruncated EHVI baseline: tox 0.83.)

A · Per-round learning curves

Performance vs AL round (mean over lines × seeds). Top — nomination quality (the final shortlist if we stopped at round r). Bottom — assayed-set quality (what's been measured so far).

A · Per-round vs end-stage filtering (does filter timing matter?)

Permissible efficacy vs AL round for per-round filtering (solid) vs a single end-stage filter (dashed). The gap widens with rounds — per-round filtering increasingly pays off as more budget would otherwise be spent on genes that get discarded.

B · Efficacy vs concentration

Each line a base; markers are operators (none / cap / k-DPP·embedding / k-DPP·CORUM). Left = better hedged; high = efficacy retained. The k-DPP·embedding vs k-DPP·CORUM gap is the similarity-source ablation (learned vs external knowledge).

B · Value of diversity — pathway-failure simulation

Portfolio value retained as the most-valuable pathways are eliminated one by one (a pathway proving non-viable). A diversified shortlist (cap / k-DPP) loses less than the concentrated baseline.
